title: Choose the smallest adaptation that can work
description: Match change rate and evidence needs to an adaptation layer, then limit rollout until evaluation and deletion drills support wider exposure.

mechanisms.label: Generic baseline
mechanisms.updatePath: Change the request or base product policy.

mechanisms.label: Request-time prompt
mechanisms.detail: Insert a few approved profile claims into the current request.
mechanisms.updatePath: Edit or remove the claim; the next request uses the new value.

mechanisms.label: Authorized retrieval
mechanisms.detail: Fetch fresh tenant or user evidence under source permissions.
mechanisms.updatePath: Revoke the source, invalidate derived chunks, and clear caches.

mechanisms.label: Versioned learned adapter
mechanisms.detail: Train a bounded behavior change from a consented example set.
mechanisms.updatePath: Retrain or retire the adapter and trace every deployed version.

scenarios.label: A writing style changes often
scenarios.brief: The user changes tone and answer length every few weeks.
scenarios.consequence: A visible prompt claim stays easy to edit; learned weights would make a changing preference unnecessarily sticky.

scenarios.label: A private handbook changes hourly
scenarios.brief: Answers must cite the user's authorized project handbook and stop using it after access is revoked.
scenarios.consequence: Retrieval preserves source identity and revocation; putting handbook facts into an adapter creates stale, hard-to-delete knowledge.

scenarios.label: A stable domain behavior remains unmet
scenarios.brief: Prompt and retrieval baselines still fail a versioned formatting protocol after enough consented examples are collected.
scenarios.consequence: A versioned adapter may be justified, but only after the lighter baselines fail and rollback, evaluation, and deletion are proven.
